How it works

    A little about you

    This tailors a few labels. Nothing is sent anywhere.

    What type of organization are you with?

      Add your courses

      A title and a few sentences per course. Name the tools, tasks and topics learners actually practice. Specific descriptions give better results.

      Bring in a whole list at once

      Pick the option that matches what you have. Each one ends with your courses listed on the left.

      A I have my courses in Excel or Google Sheets
      1. Set up three columns with these headings: code, title, description.
      2. Save it as a CSV file. In Excel: File → Save As → CSV. In Google Sheets: File → Download → .csv.
      3. Choose the file here. Your courses load into the box below.
      B My catalog is a PDF or a webpage

      Your AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Copilot) can turn it into the format this page needs. This part happens in your AI tool's chat window, in a separate tab.

      1. Copy the prompt with the button below.
      2. Open your AI tool in a new tab and paste the prompt into a new chat.
      3. Give it your catalog, in that same chat:
        • PDF: attach the file using the paperclip or + button next to the message box. If your tool can't take files, open the PDF, copy the pages for your program, and paste that text into the chat.
        • Webpage: paste the link. Some AI tools can open links and some can't. If it says it can't, copy the course text from the page and paste that instead.
      4. Send it. The AI replies with lines of text that look like code,title,description, one course per line.
      5. Copy the AI's whole reply and paste it into the box below. If the AI offers a downloadable CSV file instead, save it and use option A.
      See what the prompt says

      Analyze your courses

      Choose how to find the competencies, knowledge, tools and skills in each course. Everything maps to O*NET, so it connects to real jobs. For a fuller analysis, we recommend your own AI tool. The built-in option gives quick suggestions for a first pass. Either way, you confirm every item on the next step.

      Analysis method

      Quick suggestions (built-in)

      A fast first pass. For a fuller analysis, try your own AI tool with one of the options above.

      Connect your AI

      Your key stays in this page's memory and goes only to the provider you choose. It's never saved and is cleared when you close the tab. Your course titles and descriptions are sent to that provider for this request.

      How to get an API key

        Copy and paste with your AI

        Your course titles and descriptions go to the AI account you paste them into. Using a work account? Check with your IT team first.

        1. Copy the prompt with the button below. It already includes your courses.
        2. Open ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Copilot in a new tab and paste it into a new chat. There's nothing else to attach.
        3. The AI replies with a block of text that starts with {. Copy all of it, paste it into the box below, and click Apply.

        Tag by hand

        Go to Review and use the "+ Add" boxes under each course. Competency suggestions come from O*NET's list of work activities, so your tags still connect to jobs.

        What learners will gain

        Everything found automatically starts as a suggestion. Keep what fits, remove the rest, and add anything missing. Only kept items count in your profile, job matches and audit.

        Program profile

        Everything learners gain across your program, built from the competencies you kept.

        Jobs your courses lead to

        Ranked by how many of each occupation's work activities your courses build, plus how closely your descriptions match. Add good fits to your targets; hide the rest.

        Target jobs

        Search 900+ occupations by everyday job titles. Each target shows what the job requires and, once you add courses, what your program covers.

          Program audit

          How well your courses cover each target job, the gaps to close first, and courses no target job calls for.

          Sources

          Occupations, tasks, work activities, knowledge, skills, software and job titles: O*NET 31.0 Database (August 2026 release), U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration.

          Employment and median wages: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2025 national estimates. National figures may differ in your area.

          Typical entry education and training: BLS Employment Projections, Education and training assignments by detailed occupation (Table 5.4), 2025.
